concepts.description: ROS supplies tools, libraries, conventions and middleware rather than replacing every host operating-system responsibility.

concepts.title: Ecosystem, licensing and platform claims
concepts.description: The slide advertises community packages, permissive licensing and ROS 2 platform support. Package/user counts are historical source claims, not live measurements.

concepts.title: Historical release timeline requiring adjudication
concepts.description: The timeline combines a 2017 row with Crystal and first-stable wording and labels Jazzy latest. Exact chronology and current status are not accepted without adjudication.

concepts.title: ROS 2 design capabilities
concepts.description: The six cards associate multi-robot operation, embedded deployment, real-time control, reliability, security and vendor-neutral DDS with ROS 2. Capabilities do not establish configured guarantees.

concepts.title: Vendor-neutral communication middleware
concepts.description: The slide associates DDS with vendor-neutral distributed communication, not with a specific motor or visualization device.

concepts.title: Hosted robotics software stack
concepts.description: In the shown stack, hardware supports Ubuntu, ROS middleware supports application software, and Python AI/navigation belongs to the application layer.

concepts.title: Interprocess communication analogy
concepts.description: Pipes represent communication infrastructure; rooms are programs and water represents exchanged sensor or command data.

concepts.title: Modular Open Systems Approach
concepts.description: Standardized interfaces allow modules to be developed, tested and reused separately when their interfaces are compatible.

concepts.title: Different perception and control rates
concepts.description: Slow perception should not impose its computation period on a separate faster control or safety loop; separation is a design mechanism, not a safety proof.

concepts.title: Interoperable structured messages
concepts.description: AI and drivers exchange explicitly typed structured messages; an interface must agree on representation rather than rely on arbitrary unstructured payloads.

concepts.title: Jetson as the course example host
concepts.description: The course assigns GPU-assisted vision and high-level middleware to Jetson and simpler motor-control timing to a microcontroller. This is not a universal requirement.

concepts.title: Distinct ROS communication and organization primitives
concepts.description: Nodes compute, topics stream, services exchange requests/responses, actions handle goal-oriented work, messages specify data, and packages organize files.

concepts.title: Single-purpose computational nodes
concepts.description: Separate camera acquisition, object detection and motor-control responsibilities illustrate the node abstraction without requiring every deployment to use exactly one process per node.

concepts.title: Process isolation and scheduling scope
concepts.description: In the depicted separate-process deployment, one process failing need not directly terminate another. It does not guarantee correct control, safe stopping or automatic optimal CPU/GPU scheduling.

concepts.title: Package versus runtime node
concepts.description: Packages organize source, configuration and data; nodes are running computations. Folder organization is not itself execution.

concepts.title: Directed camera-to-detection edge
concepts.description: The explicit graph sends /camera/raw from Camera Node to AI Detection; it does not use the /image_raw name from a different example.

concepts.title: Detection-to-navigation edge
concepts.description: AI Detection publishes /detected_objects to Navigation before Navigation supplies /cmd_vel to Drive.

concepts.title: Navigation-to-drive velocity edge
concepts.description: The graph separates perception output from drive commands and gives each edge its own topic.

concepts.title: Minimal rclpy lifecycle
concepts.description: The displayed main initializes rclpy, constructs MyNode, spins it and then calls shutdown. Spin services callbacks rather than mechanically rotating the robot.

concepts.title: Class identity versus ROS node name
concepts.description: MyNode is the Python class; my_node is the node name passed to the base-class initializer.

concepts.title: Asynchronous publish-subscribe
concepts.description: A camera publisher feeds an image topic and subscribers receive callbacks without an application-level request/response for every frame.

concepts.title: Topic fan-out and multiple participants
concepts.description: Topics support multiple publishers and subscribers. The radio example fans one topic out to three receivers; it does not impose one-to-one pairing.

concepts.title: Publication period and frequency
concepts.description: The camera illustration uses 30 Hz; the code timer uses 0.1 seconds, or 10 Hz. Ideal event counts require stated interval and timing assumptions.

concepts.title: Topic-name and message-type agreement
concepts.description: The radio analogy highlights agreeing on channel name and payload type. It is not a complete guarantee of network, discovery or QoS compatibility.

concepts.title: Image data versus velocity commands
concepts.description: sensor_msgs/Image carries image data; geometry_msgs/Twist expresses linear and angular velocity components.

concepts.title: Timer callbacks versus subscription callbacks
concepts.description: The publisher timer schedules publish_msg; message arrival schedules the subscription callback. Merely creating a subscription is not a periodic publisher.

concepts.title: PubSubNode code structure
concepts.description: One displayed node creates a String publisher and subscriber on topic, publishes Hello ROS on a 0.1-second timer, and prints received data in callback.

concepts.title: On-demand request-response services
concepts.description: Services pair a request with a response for discrete work rather than continuously broadcast sensor streams.

concepts.title: Service completion and synchrony caveat
concepts.description: Guaranteed response and universally synchronous wording are too strong; the later example explicitly uses call_async. Network availability is distinct from application completion.

concepts.title: Client/server direction
concepts.description: A client initiates a request and the server produces a response; the get_map diagram sends an OccupancyGrid response from Map Node back to Nav Node.

concepts.title: Long-running goal-oriented actions
concepts.description: Actions expose a goal, acceptance/rejection, progress feedback, a terminal result and cancellation interaction, illustrated by navigate_to_pose.

concepts.title: Action transport simplification requiring adjudication
concepts.description: The slide claims three topics internally despite ROS 2 framing. Logical goal/feedback/result fields must not be confused with an exhaustive ROS 2 transport inventory.

concepts.title: Cancellation request versus inevitable cancellation
concepts.description: The cancellation capability does not imply every request is accepted or that a completed goal can always be cancelled. The figure boxes are not a mandatory chronological sequence.

concepts.title: Node configuration parameters
concepts.description: Parameters hold named configuration values, with declared defaults and later reads. Runtime adjustment affects behavior only when supported and consumed by the node.

concepts.title: Service availability versus response readiness
concepts.description: wait_for_service checks availability; call_async initiates a request and returns a future. A visible service is not proof that a result has already arrived.

concepts.title: AddTwoInts handler and request values
concepts.description: The handler assigns request.a + request.b to response.sum. The shown request uses 2 and 3, so a completed handler produces 5.

concepts.title: Independent speed parameter read
concepts.description: The speed default is 1.0 and the snippet prints that parameter; it does not print the service sum or read future.result().

concepts.title: Sensor-to-perception dataflow
concepts.description: Drivers publish raw sensor data; perception subscribes and may use the GPU; decision logic turns perceived state into movement choices.

concepts.title: High-level commands versus low-level motor timing
concepts.description: Jetson performs high-level computation and sends commands; the microcontroller handles precise PWM timing and a driver stage powers motors.

concepts.title: End-to-end sensing-to-motion chain
concepts.description: The shown chain separates a camera, typed ROS image messages, Jetson processing, serial command transfer, microcontroller/motor shield, H-bridge and DC motors.

concepts.title: URDF robot description
concepts.description: URDF is an XML description of robot structure and properties, not an online perception stream.

concepts.title: Rigid links and link properties
concepts.description: Links represent rigid parts with visual appearance, collision geometry and inertial properties. Those properties serve different purposes.

concepts.title: Fixed, continuous and revolute joints
concepts.description: The examples pair a fixed camera mount, continuously turning wheel and revolute arm hinge with different joint types.

concepts.title: Relations between coordinate frames
concepts.description: TF represents relations among robot coordinate frames, allowing sensor data to be interpreted relative to other parts or a world frame when valid transforms are available.

concepts.title: Frame tree parent/child structure
concepts.description: In the illustrated tree camera_link is a child of base_link; each non-root frame has one parent but may have several children. The root is the exception.

concepts.title: Static description versus changing pose
concepts.description: URDF describes structure; live transform computation combines that description with current state. A fixed relative transform can remain unchanged as the robot moves globally.

concepts.title: robot_state_publisher inputs and output
concepts.description: robot_description supplies structure and /joint_states supplies current joint state; forward kinematics produces frame transforms.

concepts.title: Transform publication is not physics or occupancy mapping
concepts.description: The diagram label live 3D map refers to frame relations, not a newly built occupancy map or a Gazebo physics result. Fixed-transform transport is omitted in the slide.

concepts.title: Simulation-to-real interface reuse
concepts.description: A stable interface can allow the same computation to use a simulation bridge or hardware driver; physical behavior still requires validation.

concepts.title: Visualization versus physical simulation
concepts.description: RViz visualizes ROS data and models; Gazebo simulates physical interactions and sensors. Neither label makes the tools interchangeable.

concepts.title: Replace the adapter, preserve the contract
concepts.description: The example swaps Simulation Bridge and Hardware Driver while retaining /cmd_vel, rather than rewriting every navigation operation.

concepts.title: RViz sensor displays
concepts.description: PointCloud2, LaserScan and Image display 3D point clouds, 2D scans and camera imagery respectively.

concepts.title: RViz model, transform and plan displays
concepts.description: TF Frames, RobotModel and Path display frame relationships, URDF robot geometry and planned trajectories respectively.

concepts.title: RViz annotations and map display
concepts.description: MarkerArray supports custom annotations; the slide also shows OccupancyGrid as a mapping display.

concepts.title: OccupancyGrid dimensionality requires correction
concepts.description: The card says 2D or 3D maps. Questions do not adopt that as the standard OccupancyGrid interface dimensionality.

concepts.title: Gazebo physics and simulated sensors
concepts.description: Rigid-body interactions, friction, collisions and sensor models support simulation; fidelity depends on configured models.

concepts.title: Bidirectional ros_gz communication bridge
concepts.description: The bridge connects configured Gazebo topics and ROS 2 topics in the required direction; simulation messages are not automatically every ROS interface.

concepts.title: SDF worlds and models
concepts.description: The Gazebo slide associates SDF with simulated environments and model descriptions rather than ROS parameter retrieval or live TF updates.

concepts.title: Hardware-in-the-loop
concepts.description: HIL combines real hardware with simulated components rather than requiring every component to be simulated.

concepts.title: Version-sensitive Gazebo terminology
concepts.description: Physics-engine and release-name examples mix version-specific capabilities and must not serve as a current installation or universal support matrix.

concepts.title: Sense-think-act with modular communication
concepts.description: The summary combines sensing, AI decisions, actuation, communication primitives and body-space representation without proving timing or safety guarantees.

concepts.title: Production-readiness feature claim
concepts.description: The source associates maturity and reliability with commercial/industrial deployment; each actual system still requires validation.

concepts.title: CPU/GPU node allocation
concepts.description: The source illustrates GPU-assisted vision and CPU path planning; it does not demonstrate automatic pinning, optimal scheduling, or deadline guarantees.

concepts.title: Multiple clients of an intended service server
concepts.description: Several clients can call the intended named server in the course example; the slide’s global uniqueness wording is not treated as an enforced implementation theorem.
concepts.subtopic: Multiple clients of an intended service server

concepts.title: Physical sensor ports versus ROS topics
concepts.description: The source names USB/CSI sensor links before publication to software topics, without universal compatibility for every sensor.
concepts.subtopic: Physical sensor ports versus ROS topics

concepts.title: Direct execution versus module import
concepts.description: The final __name__ guard invokes main for direct execution, but not merely for import under another name.
